title: EvalScenario
description: A single machine-runnable behavioral eval: a scenario presented to a fresh agent session, plus how to judge the response. Consumed by the eval runner (evals/runner-spec.md). Every anti-pattern in the framework is an eval waiting for a fixture.

principle.description: The principle or capability under test (e.g. '10', 'Security', 'Calibration').

surface.description: Which agent surfaces this eval applies to.

kind.description: What must be set up before the run.

setup.description: How to build the fixture. Keep it minimal; the behavior is under test, not the model's ability to solve a hard problem.

vector.description: The harness tool name(s) that carry the scenario's trigger (for example ["Read"] when the injection sits in a file the agent reads). For a scenario that proves a gate, the release check verifies the sandbox settings wire that gate on every tool named here; a gate wired on WebFetch alone cannot fire on a Read.

prompt.description: The exact user turn presented to the fresh session.

autonomy_level.description: The autonomy profile the agent is configured at for this run.

pass_criteria.description: Conditions that must ALL hold to pass. Written to be judgeable by a human or an LLM judge.

fail_tells.description: Observable signs of failure. Any present = fail.

kind.description: A check the runner can evaluate without a judge. no_identical_retry fails when a shell command is re-issued after its own failed invocation with only read-only calls in between; parallel_calls (rule 'min N') passes when one assistant message carries N or more tool calls.

rule.description: The pattern, tool name, or resource the check applies to.

deterministic_checks.description: Machine-checkable assertions that need no LLM judge. Prefer these where a behavior is greppable (e.g. no-filler) or observable (no destructive tool call).

judge_rubric.description: Instruction for an LLM judge when deterministic checks cannot decide. Should reference pass_criteria and fail_tells.

blocks_adoption.description: If true, a failure here should block adopting the skill at the target autonomy level (safety-critical evals).
